subject.title: [Bug]: clearUnboundScopes strips operator scopes unconditionally for non-local token-auth clients

question: Should device-less shared-token/password WebSocket operator clients be allowed to receive `operator.write` or stronger scopes, and should that come from client-declared scopes, configured token scopes, or a device-bound trust path?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the repair decides how much authority a network client with only the shared Gateway secret can obtain, which is a security and product boundary rather than a mechanical cleanup choice.

options.title: Bounded configured token scopes
options.body: Continue through the `gateway.auth.tokenScopes` or successor design, with explicit exposure guards, docs, upgrade behavior, and Gateway auth regression proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Trust requested scopes after shared auth
options.body: Allow valid shared-token/password WebSocket clients to retain their requested scopes directly, accepting the larger network shared-secret authority boundary.

options.title: Keep fail-closed default
options.body: Preserve scope clearing for device-less network clients and document that remote write/admin access requires pairing, tokenScopes, or another explicit trust mechanism.

recommendation.title: Bounded configured token scopes
recommendation.body: Continue through the `gateway.auth.tokenScopes` or successor design, with explicit exposure guards, docs, upgrade behavior, and Gateway auth regression proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` owns the open tokenScopes implementation candidate and has recent commits on the cleared-scope baseline, making them the best current routing target for the product/security choice.
